edges.mechanism: NAC is a sulfhydryl donor. It potentiates nitrate vasodilation (coronary and temporal artery) and the haemodynamic effects of isosorbide dinitrate, which can cause headache and hypotension.
edges.evidence: Crossover study in volunteers (headache score 3 vs 1); coronary and heart-failure studies; RCT in unstable angina (n=200) where NAC plus transdermal nitroglycerin caused intolerable headache in 35%.

edges.mechanism: Charcoal adsorbs NAC and lowers oral NAC absorption (peak -29%, AUC -39%).
edges.evidence: Crossover study in 19 subjects; PK review; FDA label for acetylcysteine solution.

edges.mechanism: NAC lowers the activity of factors II, VII, IX and X (PT/INR up 15-30%) and inhibits platelet aggregation. Bleeding risk may be additive, and NAC can also confound INR monitoring.
edges.evidence: RCT in aortic surgery with IV NAC (PT -33%, ADP aggregation down, blood loss linked to low PT); narrative review of 19 studies. No oral-supplement interaction study exists.

edges.mechanism: NAC inhibited thrombin- and ADP-induced platelet aggregation in vitro at concentrations reachable orally, so antiplatelet effects may be additive.
edges.evidence: In vitro study in type-2 diabetes blood plus a surgical RCT; no clinical interaction study; very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: In IPF, the triple regimen of prednisone, azathioprine and NAC increased death (8 vs 1) and hospitalisation (23 vs 7) compared with placebo.
edges.evidence: PANTHER-IPF RCT; the triple-therapy arm was stopped early.

edges.mechanism: NAC replenishes glutathione to detoxify NAPQI and is the standard antidote. Overdose needs protocol-based medical dosing, not supplement doses.
edges.evidence: Cochrane review, RCTs of regimens (SARPO non-inferior 12-h regimen), FDA labels.

edges.mechanism: Both are used as insulin sensitizers in PCOS. Head-to-head MAs show similar pregnancy rates, with NAC lowering BMI and testosterone. No data exist on combined use, so effects may overlap.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs comparing NAC vs metformin; no combination interaction study.

edges.mechanism: Glycine and cysteine (from NAC) are both glutathione precursors. GlyNAC corrected GSH deficiency and oxidative stress in older adults in Sekhar trials. A larger 2-week RCT missed its primary GSH end point.
edges.evidence: Small RCT (n=24) and pilot; RCT (n=114) null on primary outcome; very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Combined antioxidant use (NAC or vitamin E) reduced ROS/p53 and accelerated lung tumour progression in mouse models.
edges.evidence: Preclinical (mouse) only; relevance to humans is unknown.

edges.mechanism: Adding ascorbic acid to NAC gave no additional prevention of contrast-induced nephropathy.
edges.evidence: MA of 6 RCTs (n=919).

edges.mechanism: The combined product contains NAC, so taking it with standalone NAC duplicates the NAC dose. GI adverse events rose with dose (more GI events at 2,400 mg/d).
edges.evidence: Dose-related side-effect trend in an MA; youth RCT GI events 63/98 vs 37/94.

edges.mechanism: Inhaled acetylcysteine can trigger bronchospasm. Asthma/atopy raises the risk of anaphylactoid reactions to IV NAC.
edges.evidence: FDA labels (inhalation solution, Acetadote); systematic review of adverse reactions.

edges.mechanism: Non-IgE histamine-mediated reactions (rash, angioedema, bronchospasm, hypotension) occurred in 8.2% of IV courses; anaphylaxis 0.1-0.2%.
edges.evidence: Large Canadian cohort (6,455 courses); FDA label.

edges.mechanism: NAC monotherapy did not preserve FVC. Any benefit may be confined to TOLLIP rs3750920 TT carriers.
edges.evidence: PANTHER RCT (n=264); post hoc pharmacogenetic analysis.

edges.mechanism: In IPF, NAC was associated with benefit in TT carriers (HR 0.14) and a trend toward harm in CC carriers (HR 3.23).
edges.evidence: Post hoc PANTHER analysis replicated in an independent cohort; prospective PRECISIONS trial under way.

edges.with: lung cancer or high lung-cancer risk (smokers)
edges.mechanism: Antioxidant NAC accelerated lung-tumour progression and induced adenocarcinoma in aged or JunD-deficient mice.
edges.evidence: Preclinical only; no human outcome data.

edges.mechanism: NAC blunted redox-sensitive signalling (mTOR/p70S6K/p38) and delayed strength recovery after eccentric exercise. It does not improve performance.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCT (n=10); MA of 7 studies (+0.29%, NS).

edges.mechanism: Anticoagulant and platelet-inhibiting effects of NAC; low PT values were associated with greater blood loss.
edges.evidence: RCT in abdominal aortic aneurysm repair with IV NAC.

edges.mechanism: NAC falsely lowers creatinine without changing cystatin C, more with non-Jaffe assays and IV dosing. This can mimic renoprotection.
edges.evidence: SR of 6 studies (n=199): WMD -3.24 umol/L (non-Jaffe), -31.10 umol/L (IV); Trinder assay study.

edges.with: Trinder-based assays (triglycerides, cholesterol, uric acid, HDL/LDL-C)
edges.mechanism: NAC inhibits the peroxidase (Trinder) reaction and gives falsely low results. Inhibition of >=10% occurred at 570-2,900 mg/L, above concentrations expected with therapy.
edges.evidence: In vitro study on Roche cobas assays plus a retrospective chart review.

edges.mechanism: NAC raises PT/INR by 15-30% (lower factor II/VII/IX/X activity plus an in vitro effect over time), independent of liver injury.
edges.evidence: Narrative review of 19 studies; in vitro studies.
